title: Death abroad or far from home: distance, consulate, translation, repatriation, and not being able to get there

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source and seed-brief synthesis for rev0020 absence / official-trace layer; no private testimony, no public rendering, no forensic/legal/search advice.
source_packet.collection_method: manual public-source extraction, source-card routing, and seed-cue factoring during rev0020
limitations: Public and official sources support vocabulary, context, and review routing only; they do not supply consented bedside testimony.
Official-record material is jurisdiction-dependent and must not be universalized into legal or forensic advice.
Records must not advise families how to investigate a death, identify remains, handle bodies, claim property, notify kin, or interpret cause/manner of death.

moment.plain_scene: Some families meet death through distance: another country, another state, a disaster site, a body not yet released, translated papers, consular language, or a funeral that cannot wait.
ordinary_language_queries: loved one died far away cannot get body
body returned home after death abroad

content_layers.observation_text: Some families meet death through distance: another country, another state, a disaster site, a body not yet released, translated papers, consular language, or a funeral that cannot wait.
content_layers.source_synthesis: The sources support treating this as a recurring absence/official-trace pattern around death, identification, body custody, and family waiting, while keeping authority, timing, procedures, and rights dependent on local law, office policy, culture, and professional review.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: For DeathVocab, absence is not empty. A missing witness, missing body, missing name, missing family, or pending certificate changes what can be known, mourned, searched, claimed, or said.
interpretation.public_rendering_rule: Render as witnessed language and boundary grammar only; never as forensic procedure, legal advice, investigative guidance, or institutional finality.

what_this_is_not: a public identification or search tool
a judgment about whether anyone cared
uncertainties: Local law, office policy, disaster conditions, family structure, and identification status may change the meaning of the record.
Official documents can stabilize some facts while leaving human experience, relationship, ritual need, and meaning unresolved.
content_layers.lay_orientation: Some deaths leave families with more paperwork than scene, more case number than witness, or more waiting than goodbye. The archive must name that without pretending it can resolve it.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: Future work should route this record through official-trace, privacy, legal/jurisdictional, grief, and non-voyeurism review before any public rendering.
language_notes: Keep official terms, family terms, and archive interpretation separate.
Use decedent/remains/body/person with care; preserve personhood while respecting source language.
Avoid closure language where there is no body, no identification, or no final certificate.

provenance.provenance_statement: Added in rev0020 from public-source synthesis and seed-cue factoring; no private account, no official validation, no legal validation, no public release.

safety.identifiability_boundary: Do not include names, dates, rare locations, case details, images, database screenshots, personal effects, family contact details, or unusual circumstances that could identify a person or family.
safety.medical_advice_risk: Do not use this record to determine cause of death, manner of death, prognosis, infectious risk, body condition, viewing suitability, or clinical procedure.
safety.legal_or_facility_advice_risk: Do not infer reporting duties, next-of-kin authority, claim rights, release timing, autopsy rights, property rights, registration rules, or investigation strategy from this record.
safety.cultural_or_ritual_risk: Do not treat official delay, missing remains, or public disposition as culturally neutral; route ritual and tradition impacts to tradition-holder review.
safety.clinical_boundary: This is not clinical, forensic, legal, emergency, public-health, funeral, or death-investigation advice; local qualified authorities govern actual cases.
safety_notes: Absence records are high risk for identifiability, stigma, public speculation, and institutional overclaim.
Do not turn database/search vocabulary into amateur investigation or public identification attempts.
Do not treat lack of witness, lack of claim, or delayed identification as evidence of lack of love.
